title: You Enter University to Study Computer Science — But Are You Ready for the Future?

meta.tone: Professional, warm, inspiring, slightly thought-provoking. Never scolding, never hype.

protagonist.name: Tharindu
protagonist.role: First-year Computer Science undergraduate, Sri Lanka
protagonist.visual_anchor: 19-year-old Sri Lankan student, warm brown skin, short black wavy hair, thin silver-rimmed glasses, pale blue short-sleeve collared shirt, dark navy canvas backpack, simple white canvas shoes
protagonist.arc: Nervous and excited first-year (Act 1) to composed, curious, capable young technologist (Act 3). Posture opens, gaze lifts, clothing shifts from uniform-like neatness to relaxed practitioner.

style.base: High-quality cinematic 3D animation, feature-film lighting, physically based rendering, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, smooth motivated camera moves, 16:9 anamorphic framing

A.look: Grounded, warm, recognisably South Asian / Sri Lankan. Tropical daylight, ochre and terracotta walls, deep green foliage, ceiling fans, chalk-dusted whiteboards, worn wooden desks, corridor light shafts. NO Silicon Valley glass towers.
A.palette: Warm ochre #C98A3C, terracotta #A9502F, foliage green #2F5D3A, chalk white #F2EDE3, sky #9FC7DE

B.look: Hybrid. The real campus remains, but translucent cyan holographic data layers grow inside it. Physical and digital coexist in the same frame.
B.palette: Warm base carried over, plus holo cyan #4FD8E8, signal amber #F2A93B, deep teal #0E3B45

C.look: Futuristic and global, but never sterile. Volumetric light, deep indigo voids, suspended geometry, quantum shimmer. Warmth returns in the final sunrise.
C.palette: Deep indigo #131A3A, quantum violet #7A5CF0, holo cyan #4FD8E8, sunrise gold #F5B95C

style.negative: No photorealistic live action, no Western/Silicon Valley campus tropes in Act A, no exaggerated sci-fi weaponry, no readable fake logos or brand marks, no dense unreadable UI text, no cluttered on-screen typography, no depiction of any language or technology as dead or obsolete

audio.music: Single evolving orchestral-electronic cue. Act A: solo piano + light strings + subtle tabla-adjacent percussion. Act B: pulse and arpeggios enter, tempo climbs. Act C: full strings + synth pads. FINAL: resolve to warm major, then a single sustained piano note over the end card.
audio.sfx: Campus ambience (birds, distant chatter, ceiling fan, chalk, keyboard), holographic whooshes on transitions, low sub-bass hits on act changes, silence beat before the AI-plagiarism warning and before the final title.
audio.mix: Narration -3 dB peak, music ducked to -18 dB under narration, full at transitions.

scenes.name: COLD OPEN / MAIN TITLE
scenes.intent: Establish place before message. Sri Lanka first, question second.

shots.camera: Slow aerial descent through palm and mara tree canopy toward a university campus at early morning
shots.action: Mist over a South Asian campus. Red-tiled roofs, whitewashed colonnades, a cricket ground edge, distant hills.
shots.prompt: Cinematic 3D animation, slow aerial descent through tropical palm and rain-tree canopy at 6am, revealing a Sri Lankan university campus below: red clay-tiled roofs, whitewashed colonnaded buildings, green quadrangle, distant blue hills, morning mist and golden god-rays, birds crossing frame, warm ochre and deep green palette, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, feature-film lighting, 16:9

shots.camera: Locked wide, slow push in
shots.action: Main title card resolves over the campus gate as light blooms behind it.
onscreen: YOU ENTER UNIVERSITY TO STUDY COMPUTER SCIENCE
BUT ARE YOU READY FOR THE FUTURE?
shots.prompt: Cinematic 3D animation, static wide shot of an ornate South Asian university entrance gate in golden morning light, slow push in, lens flare blooming behind the gate arch, empty clean sky above for title typography, warm ochre and green palette, shallow depth of field, film grain, 16:9

scenes.name: THE FIRST DAY
scenes.intent: Warmth and excitement. The audience should like this student immediately.
vo: You have entered university to study Computer Science.
You may believe that the next three or four years will teach you everything you need to become a software engineer.
But there is something you need to understand from day one.
Computer Science is one of the fastest-changing fields in the world.

shots.camera: Slow arc around the student, reverse to reveal their face

scenes.name: THE UNIVERSITY EXPERIENCE
scenes.intent: Respectful, accurate portrait of the degree. Foundations framed as genuinely valuable.
vo: Your university will give you something extremely valuable: foundations.
You will learn algorithms, databases, operating systems, networking, software engineering, mathematics and computer science theory.
You will eventually complete a major project.
But your degree is not the finish line.

scenes.name: THE TECHNOLOGY TIMELINE
scenes.intent: First 'wow' beat. The world speeds up around a still student.
vo: Technology does not wait for your university syllabus.
Cloud computing changes how applications are built.
Artificial intelligence is changing how software itself is created.

shots.camera: Push in on the desk, then lift
shots.action: A holographic line of light ignites across the lecture hall and pierces the far wall.

scenes.name: JAVA TO PYTHON — CONCEPTS TRANSFER
scenes.intent: Critical nuance: Java is respected, not buried. Concepts are the durable asset.
vo: Learning one programming language teaches you concepts that transfer to others.
But do not make the mistake of believing that mastering one language means you have mastered programming.

shots.camera: Over-the-shoulder, screen glow on face
shots.action: The student writes Java in a traditional IDE. Focused, methodical, satisfied.

shots.camera: Continuous orbit, environment swaps around the solids

scenes.name: WEB DEVELOPMENT EVOLVES
scenes.intent: Dramatic single continuous morph. One website becomes a modern distributed system.
vo: Do not spend your entire university journey learning yesterday's development stack.
Can I build something with it?

scenes.name: THE AI EXPLOSION
scenes.intent: AI as a family of technologies, not one magic object. Structure over spectacle.
vo: Artificial Intelligence is not one single technology.
It is a family of technologies.
And increasingly, AI agents capable of using tools and performing tasks.

scenes.name: MATHEMATICS AND STATISTICS
scenes.intent: Deliberate slow-down. The most 'unfashionable' scene should be the most beautiful.
vo: And here is something many students discover too late.
You may wonder why you need them when modern libraries can perform the calculations for you.
But you need to understand what the calculation means.
If you want to move beyond simply using AI tools and start understanding AI, data science and machine learning, mathematics and statistics become powerful foundations.

scenes.name: THEORY AND APPLICATION
scenes.intent: Two paths converge. Theory is never mocked — it is one of two rails.
vo: But theory without application can leave you unprepared.
Your goal should not simply be:
'I understand the concept — and I can use it to solve a real problem.'

scenes.name: THE MARKET EXPECTATION
scenes.intent: The world opens up. Campus becomes globe — the one moment we go global.
vo: The technology industry does not simply ask:
'Can you use AI effectively without losing your ability to think?'

shots.camera: Continuous pull back through the classroom wall

shots.prompt: Cinematic 3D animation, continuous camera pull back as the walls of a warm South Asian classroom dissolve into light and open out into a vast global network space, the desks becoming distant illuminated city clusters, seamless single-take feeling, warm ochre transitioning into cyan and indigo, volumetric light, film grain, 16:9

scenes.name: AI AND ACADEMIC INTEGRITY
scenes.intent: The moral centre. Show the failure honestly, then the correct workflow. Never shame the student.
vo: You can now generate an essay.
Even generate an entire project structure.
But there is a dangerous shortcut:
using AI without understanding what it produces.
AI should accelerate learning — not replace learning.
Use AI as a tutor, coding assistant, reviewer and brainstorming partner.
But make sure you can explain what you submit.
Otherwise, you may pass an assignment while failing to develop the skill the assignment was supposed to teach.

shots.camera: Static medium, mood cools
shots.action: An assignment brief lands on the desk. Light shifts cooler; music thins.

scenes.intent: The most actionable scene. Concrete, year by year, do-this-tomorrow.
vo: Do not wait until your final year to build your portfolio.
Your GitHub repositories, projects and practical experience can become evidence of what you actually know.

scenes.name: THE SPEED OF TECHNOLOGY
scenes.intent: Honest about uncertainty. 'Future — unknown' must feel exciting, not frightening.
vo: The technology you learn in your first year may not be the technology you use when you graduate.
Your most important skill is not memorising today's technology.
It is learning how to learn tomorrow's technology.

shots.camera: Fast lateral flight along the returning timeline
shots.action: The timeline returns and accelerates hard through recent history.
shots.prompt: Cinematic 3D animation, fast lateral flight along a returning glowing holographic timeline, year markers rushing past with increasing speed and motion blur, the gaps between markers visibly compressing as the camera accelerates, cyan and violet, heavy volumetric haze, film grain, 16:9

shots.camera: Continued acceleration to near-blur

shots.camera: Abrupt stop at the edge of the light

shots.note: Bright, not black. Uncertainty framed as opportunity.

shots.camera: Wide, student small before a shifting landscape

scenes.name: QUANTUM COMPUTING
scenes.intent: Wonder with intellectual honesty. Emerging, uncertain, worth watching. No overclaiming.
vo: And there is another technology worth watching.
It is still an emerging field, and its practical impact remains uncertain.
But if quantum computing reaches the level where it can solve important real-world problems at scale, it could create an entirely new chapter in computing.
Perhaps one day, your final-year project will not simply be another web application.
Perhaps you will explore a quantum computing problem.
If the technology matures enough — and if you are prepared — you could be part of that journey.

shots.camera: Slow push toward a single classical bit

shots.prompt: Cinematic 3D animation, slow push toward a single solid metallic cube suspended in dark space flipping crisply and definitively between two discrete states with a clean mechanical snap, precise and orderly, cool white light on deep indigo, volumetric light, film grain, 16:9

shots.camera: The cube dissolves into a sphere; slow orbit

scenes.name: THE MESSAGE TO THE STUDENT
scenes.intent: Emotional payoff. Same student, same campus, transformed capability. Earned optimism.
vo: You came to university to study Computer Science.
Do not leave with only a degree.
Leave with the ability to learn.
Leave knowing how to solve problems.
Leave understanding mathematics, data and technology.
Because the biggest technology you will learn at university may not be a programming language.
It may be the ability to adapt.
The future of computing has not been written yet.
Perhaps you will help write it.
